skill.name: technical-decision-record
skill.description: Guides teams through structured technical decision making and creates Architecture Decision Records with context, options, consequences, and reversibility.
skill.summary: Create Architecture Decision Records that document options, rationale, consequences, and reversal cost.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive: SKILL.md line 76 is a fenced Markdown template, not shell execution. No evidence found for prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or business logic abuse in the reviewed skill content.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged line is the opening fence of a Markdown ADR template, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md contains prompt instructions and static documentation only, with no executable shell command path.

content.value_statement: Teams lose context when technical choices are made without a durable record. This skill creates clear ADRs that capture options, rationale, consequences, and reversal cost.
actual_capabilities: Structures technical decisions into a standard ADR format.
Prompts for context, constraints, options, deciders, and dates.
Compares technology choices with pros, cons, cost, and effort.
Documents positive outcomes, negative consequences, risks, and mitigations.
Captures how difficult a decision will be to reverse later.
Identifies common ADR mistakes such as missing stakeholders or skipped options.
limitations: It cannot validate facts without accurate project context from the user.
It does not execute code, inspect repositories, or test architecture choices.
It cannot replace team review or stakeholder approval.
It does not maintain an ADR index across multiple documents.

use_cases.title: Choose a Database
use_cases.description: Compare candidate databases and document the final selection with constraints, trade-offs, risks, and migration impact.

use_cases.title: Record an Architecture Change
use_cases.description: Capture why a service boundary, integration pattern, or infrastructure approach changed, including consequences for future teams.

use_cases.title: Align Stakeholders
use_cases.description: Prepare a clear decision record that helps product, security, and engineering teams review the same trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single technical decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an ADR for [decision]. Ask me for missing context before drafting the record.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Notes into an ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for rough notes or meeting output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these notes into an ADR: [notes]. Include context, constraints, options, decision, consequences, risks, and reversibility.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Technical Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a decision with several viable choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these options for [decision]: [options]. Build an ADR that highlights trade-offs, stakeholder impact, and reversal cost.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for improving a drafted decision record.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ADR for gaps: [ADR text]. Identify missing constraints, weak reasoning, unaddressed risks, and stakeholder questions.

output_examples.input: We need to choose PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, or MongoDB for user profile data.
output_examples.output: A completed ADR with context, constraints, three options, the selected database, consequences, risks, and reversal cost.

output_examples.input: Our team is moving from synchronous service calls to event-driven integration.
output_examples.output: A decision record that explains the trigger, compares integration patterns, and documents operational risks for observability and retries.

output_examples.input: Review this draft ADR about adopting a third-party search service.
output_examples.output: A review summary that flags missing cost limits, data residency concerns, rollback planning, and required stakeholder approvals.

best_practices: Provide real constraints before asking for a final recommendation.
List at least two viable options, including the current approach when relevant.
Treat accepted ADRs as history and supersede them instead of rewriting them.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for an ADR after the team already ignored all alternatives.
Do not hide affected stakeholders from the decision record.
Do not spend heavy review time on decisions that are easy to reverse.

faq.question: Does this skill create Architecture Decision Records?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the user through context, constraints, options, decision, consequences, risks, and reversibility.

faq.question: Can it choose the best technology by itself?
faq.answer: No. It helps compare options, but it needs accurate constraints and team context from the user.

faq.question: Can it review an existing ADR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify missing context, weak reasoning, unaddressed risks, and unclear stakeholder involvement.

faq.question: Does it run commands or inspect project files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only and provides a documentation framework.

faq.question: What decisions fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits technology choices, architecture changes, service selection, process changes, and decisions with long-term trade-offs.

faq.question: How should old ADRs be updated?
faq.answer: Old ADRs should remain unchanged. Create a new ADR that supersedes the earlier record and explains the change.
